summary.name: Ionic Framework
summary.one_liner: Ionic is an open-source UI toolkit for building cross-platform mobile, web, and progressive web apps using web technologies and React, Angular, Vue, or no framework.
keywords: ios and android app from web code
use_cases: Build a single codebase app for iOS, Android, and web
Create a progressive web app from existing web code
Deploy mobile apps to the Apple App Store and Google Play
Access native device features like camera or geolocation from JavaScript
Prototype mobile UIs in the browser
summary.what_it_does: Ionic provides a set of UI components (such as sliders, alerts, chips, checkboxes, toggles, and inputs) that are styled with iOS and Material Design themes and adapt to the platform they run on. It works with Angular, React, Vue, or plain JavaScript, and includes a CLI, a VS Code extension, and on-device hot refresh for development. Apps are deployed to iOS and Android app stores through the Capacitor bridge, which gives access to native device plugins. The page also mentions Ionic Appflow for cloud builds, live updates, and automated store publishing.
notable: Single shared codebase for iOS, Android, and web via Capacitor
Framework-agnostic: works with Angular, React, Vue, or none
Over 100 UI components with iOS and Material Design themes and light/dark mode
Listed on awesome-mac under hybrid app frameworks; GitHub repo is driftyco/ionic
caveats: Appflow cloud builds and live updates are part of Ionic's paid service; the page does not state pricing details
Page is mostly marketing with testimonials and community stats; no specific limitations are stated
